title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The notes 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets' continue the Longue Marche programme. Here 𝔊 is a profinite group, essentially a quotient of the profinite cartographic group, with distinguished generators ρ and σ (order-2 and order-3 type elements, as in PSL2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3). 𝔊^+ is an augmented or oriented version of 𝔊. Z_{ρ,σ} is a group of quadruples u = (u, μ, ε2, ε3), where u ∈ Aut(𝔊^+), μ ∈ Ẑ* is a cyclotomic-type exponent and ε2, ε3 are twisting data. Its elements are automorphisms that normalize a subgroup L_0 and send ξ_ρ, ξ_σ to conjugates of ρ, σ in a twisted coset 𝔊^?_τ. From Z_{ρ,σ} one builds the groups G_{ρ,σ}, M_{ρ,σ}, etc. These form a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-like 'level 𝔊' symmetry group together with its natural extensions.

This page opens §6 'Fonctorialités'. A marginal NB records that §§1–5 never used the hypothesis that ρ, σ generate 𝔊^+.

Setup. Take a surjective homomorphism φ: 𝔊 → 𝔊' (91). Grothendieck adds that the same works for 𝔊_0 → 𝔊 (cf. p. 643' §4). Assume φ maps the distinguished subgroup 𝔊^? into 𝔊'^?. Primed letters (Z', M', ...) denote the objects built from 𝔊'.

Compatibility condition. As in p. 588, but now dropping the Ξ^𝔊_{ρ,σ} part, the condition says: for every u ∈ Z_{ρ,σ} there is an automorphism u' of 𝔊'^+ with φ∘u = u'∘φ (diagram 92). Since φ is surjective, u' is unique.

Equivalent form. Every automorphism of 𝔊^+ coming from Z_{ρ,σ} must stabilize ker φ. These are the automorphisms that normalize L_0 and send ξ_ρ, ξ_σ to elements of 𝔊_τ conjugate to ρ, σ.

Consequences (next page). One gets a homomorphism Z_{ρ,σ} → Z_{ρ',σ'} (93), compatible with the actions and with the maps from L_0. By the standard construction this gives homomorphisms of the G-groups (94–95). Hence all diagrams of the preceding sections, written for (ρ,σ), map to those for (ρ',σ'). In short, the 'GT at level 𝔊' construction is functorial for surjections whose kernel is stable under the level-𝔊 symmetries.
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence 'u descends to 𝔊'^+ iff u(ker φ) ⊆ ker φ' implicitly uses that Z_{ρ,σ} is a group, so u^{-1} also stabilizes the kernel and u' is an automorphism. This holds automatically for open kernels by an index argument; Grothendieck leaves it implicit.

The superscript on 𝔊 in 'φ applique 𝔊^? dans 𝔊'^?' is ambiguous. It cannot really be 'φ', since φ is only being introduced. It is probably the same distinguished-subgroup symbol used on the previous page (𝔊^𝔊 / M^G).

ideas.what: Functoriality of the symmetry groups Z_{ρ,σ}, G_{ρ,σ}, M_{ρ,σ} under surjections 𝔊 → 𝔊' of marked profinite (cartographic-type) groups. The condition is that ker φ is stable under all automorphisms in Z_{ρ,σ}.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility / descent of GT-type automorphisms to characteristic-like quotients; the transition maps in the system of 'GT-shadows' indexed by finite quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Level-wise approximations of GT: Harbater–Schneps, Lochak–Schneps (1990s); GT-shadows: V. Dolgushev and collaborators (2021–)
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse or the published parts of the Longue Marche in this form, as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Observation that the hypothesis 'ρ, σ generate 𝔊^+' was not needed in §§1–5 and enters only for functoriality and uniqueness questions.
ideas.modern_name: Working with non-generating marked elements, i.e. dessins/maps on a subgroup

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up GT-like symmetry groups attached to each marked quotient 𝔊 of the cartographic group. He then makes them functorial along surjections whose kernel is stable under those symmetries. This is structurally the projective system later rediscovered as 'GT-shadows' (Dolgushev et al.), which approximates GT through finite quotients.
missed.quote: les u ∈ Aut(𝔊^+) qui proviennent de Z_{ρ,σ}, i.e. qui normalisent L_0, et qui transforment ξ_ρ, ξ_σ en des éléments 𝔊_τ conjugués à ρ, σ, stabilisent le noyau de φ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precursor of the finite-level approach to GT and to the Galois action on dessins. The analogy is structural; the technical content on this page is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A standard functoriality and descent argument, step 6 of a long technical development. It is interesting only as a historical precursor of the level-wise (GT-shadow) viewpoint, with no new theorem on the page.
transcription_corrections: Diagram (92): the bottom row should read 𝔊^+ —φ→ 𝔊'^+, not '𝔊^{++} —φ'→'. Vertical arrows are u and u'.
'il existe un u[?] u' de 𝔊'' should read 'il existe un automorphisme u' de 𝔊'^+'.
The label next to 𝔊 → 𝔊' is (91), matching the later reference 'noyau de φ (91)'.
The 'Il va de même avec 𝔊_0 → 𝔊 cf p. 643' §4' passage is a right-margin insertion.
The superscript in '𝔊^φ' / '𝔊'^φ' is uncertain. It is likely the same G-type symbol used as a superscript on the previous page, not φ.
'On a des conditions équivalentes' should read 'On a des conditions équivalentes (comme dans loc. cit ...)'. The Ξ is Ξ^{𝔊}_{ρ,σ}.
